items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: This was the band, you know, with Buddy Smith and Junior Mance and myself and Griff

ctx.x: Did that band ever make a record?

The band? Yes, it did. Only Clean Head wasn't on it. This was the band, you know, with Buddy Smith and Junior Mance and myself and Griff -- they had a disc jockey in Chicago, oh, he was very popular at that time. Al Benson. He come by the club and told Griff Red he wanted us to record. For him.

And so we said okay, and we go by the next day -- we go by Al's house, he had a home over on the South Side, in his basement, and he says he had a couple of tunes he's gonna fix. Al paid us off -- they made about $50 a piece -- and we recorded the next day after we rehearsed it, and I think they released that about '56 or '57 -- I think Al Benson had a tie up with the Chess Brothers, and I think it came out on Chess Records or Veejay -- I don't know which one -- but it was called "JG", and ...
